texto: Economic growth and energy availability walk together. Consequently, the construction of hydropower plants and transmission lines are beneficial and essential to Brazil’s development. The gains from implementing such projects outweigh their potential negative impacts. Some of these benefits are low cost for energy generation, obtaining energy from a renewable sustainable source and developing programs that are important to preserve the environment in the region, creating new jobs and strengthening the local economy. Aligned with its commitment to the sustainable development of the communities where it operates, all Alupar projects are in compliance with the environmental laws based on the instruments and rites of the process of environmental licensing, and follow the resolutions of the National Environment Council (CONAMA). Each project has unique characteristics that are respected and taken into account during the Environmental Impact Study (EIA), so as to establish the most effective plan of action for each location. Based on this analysis, the Company develops programs for the preservation and recovery of Environmental Protection Areas, maintenance of the biodiversity of the fauna and flora, replacement and recovery of the native forests, maintenance of the quality of the water bodies, as well as other environmental compensations reverted to the maintenance of Conservation Units. These initiatives that aim to mitigate each project’ impacts are described in detail in the Basic Environmental Plan (PBA). Another initiative that contributes to the sustainability of Alupar’s energy generation projects is the certification to generate carbon credits which are traded on the international market. Created by the United Nations (UN), this practice is part of the Clean Development Mechanism (CDM) and highlights the contribution of the projects to reduce greenhouse gas emissions and control global warming. Fauna and Flora Maintenance of biodiversity Environment Replacement and recovery of native forests Water Maintenance of the quality of the water bodies

texto: Green Bonds are bonds issued to raise funds for projects or assets that have a positive socio-environmental impact. These bonds, which are generally long-term, attract investors committed to the development and improvement of climate issues. In December 2019, TSM – Transmissora Serra da Mantiqueira S.A., a subsidiary of Alupar, issued a green bond to finance the construction of the asset. This issuance is considered green, based on satisfactory socio-environmental performance, assessed by an independent expert opinion, and considering its contribution to the transmission of renewable energy. texto: HPP São José Alupar controls the HPP São José, placed in Rio Ijuí, in the Municipal Districts of Salvador das Missões and Rolador, in the Brazilian State of Rio Grande do Sul, with installed capacity of 51.0 MW. The concession to operate the HPP São José is valid for 35 years from the date of the concession agreement’s signature, firmed in 2006. The HPP São José has started their operations on March, 2011. Each turbine has a generation potential of 25.5 MW, totalizing a installed capacity of 51.0 MW. HPP Foz do Rio Claro Alupar controls the Foz do Rio Claro Hydroelectric Plant, located on the Rio Claro, in the municipalities of Caçu and São Simão, in Goiás state, which has an installed capacity of 68.4 MW. The concession to explore the Foz do Rio Claro facility runs for 35 years as of the date on which the concession contract was signed in 2006. The plant began operations in August, 2010. HPP Ferreira Gomes Alupar holds control of the Ferreira Gomes Hydropower Plant, which is located on the Araguari River, in the city of Ferreira Gomes, Amapá State. The plant has 252.0 MW of installed capacity. The concession to operate the Ferreira Gomes Hydroelectric Plant will be valid for 35 years from the date of the concession contract, which took place in September, 2010. The plant went into operation in November 2014, anticipating the commercial operation in relation to the date stipulated in the concession agreement. HPP La Virgen Alupar holds a 65% interest in La Virgen S.A.C., which has a license to explore the La Virgen HPP, located in the district of Chanchamayo, in Peru, with an installed capacity of 84.0 MW. Start-up is scheduled for 2017 and the concession was granted for life. Energy is traded with independent consumers and the volume of assured energy is 49.3 MW.

texto: Alupar supports Programa Expedição (Expedition program), which is part of Vaga Lume, a non-profit association focused on educational, cultural and environmental projects. The initiative provides access to books and promotes reading habits among residents of communities located in the Legal Brazilian Amazon. The program consists of three actions: donation of the physical space where the community library will operate, training of volunteers who will mediate the reading, and encouraging the community for managing its own library. The project also encourages residents to produce handmade books, as a means to value the local culture. Participants register themselves and then provide illustrations to the story, thus contributing to the library’s collection. This is one of the many programs maintained by Alupar in this area. The Company also sponsors the musical education project of Fundação Bachiana Filarmônica (Bachiana Philharmonic Foundation), developed in association with conductor João Carlos Martins in the Paraisópolis community, located in the city of São Paulo. In addition, communities in the states of Pará, Maranhão and Minas Gerais participated in the project Mestres do Futuro, a project that recovers crafting techniques on the brink of extinction. Under this program, craftsmen are trained to impart their knowledge to youth groups in the community. In exchange, they receive not only income, but also respect for their work. In many municipalities where Alupar operates, the population attended a free theater play whose content is based on the region’s cultural characteristics, with environmental issues as background. The program, which is called Arte na Comunidade (Art in the community), invites local theater companies to perform the play and travel around many cities, under the arena theater model (a circular stage with seating surrounding it), so as to reach the largest possible audience. The play’s content also becomes a game which is then distributed to the local schools, raising awareness of students about environmental issues. These programs are developed through tax incentive under the Rouanet Law. texto: Adjacent to the Verdescola Institute, located in the city of São Sebastião, state of São Paulo, is Verdesporte, a sports center supported by Alupar. Social and educational projects, including income generation and professional training programs, are also developed at the center. Additionally, the Company helps maintain a multi-purpose sports court located in the city Belo Horizonte, state of Minas Gerais. Athletes can also count on Alupar’s support. The Company sponsors the Brazilian Rugby Confederation, aiming to promote the sport in Brazil. Students with regular school attendance and good grades are invited to join the Ju-Jitsu team. texto: A good relationship with the community in the region where a new Alupar project will be implemented also depends on respect for its past history. Before starting the works, an archeological team studies the records and documents related to the region’s ancestors. After this preliminary study, the team goes to the field with the appropriate tools and thoroughly searches the project’s area of influence. If an archaeological site is found, the archaeologists begin a process of recovery, preventing any potential damages caused by the project’s implementation and deepening their knowledge about the people who lived in the region. The archeological remains are analyzed and prepared to complement collections of the period. The work is followed by IPHAN, the Institute for National Historic and Artistic Heritage, and is also part of the environmental licensing process. texto: Respect for the past history and opinion of the local communities is essential during each stage of implementation and operation of a project. For this reason, Alupar maintains an open communication channel through Social Communication Programs which are essential to information exchange between the Company and the community, so that everyone is aware of the most important events related to Alupar’s projects, ensuring transparency in any news of public interest. The project must be beneficial to all parties involved—based on this premise and the specific needs of each region, Alupar invests in programs to actively help improve quality of life in the local communities. Besides developing projects geared towards key topics, such as health and education, the Company offers strategic support and financial aid to vaccination campaigns and the expansion of health centers and schools. Through tax incentive laws, the community also benefits from cultural programs, including travelling theatre and maintenance of community libraries and multi-purpose sports centers. texto: Economic growth and energy availability walk together. Consequently, the construction of hydropower plants and transmission lines are beneficial and essential to Brazil’s development. The gains from implementing such projects outweigh their potential negative impacts. Some of these benefits are low cost for energy generation, obtaining energy from a renewable sustainable source and developing programs that are important to preserve the environment in the region, creating new jobs and strengthening the local economy. Aligned with its commitment to the sustainable development of the communities where it operates, all Alupar projects are in compliance with the environmental laws based on the instruments and rites of the process of environmental licensing, and follow the resolutions of the National Environment Council (CONAMA). Each project has unique characteristics that are respected and taken into account during the Environmental Impact Study (EIA), so as to establish the most effective plan of action for each location. Environmental Programs Replacement and Recovery of the Native Forests Preservation and Recovery of Environmental Protection Areas Maintenance of the biodiversity of the Fauna and Flora Environmental Compensations reverted to the Maintenance of Conservation Units These initiatives that aim to mitigate each project’ impacts are described in detail in the Basic Environmental Plan (PBA). Carbon Credits Another initiative that contributes to the sustainability of Alupar’s energy generation projects is the certification to generate carbon credits which are traded on the international market. Created by the United Nations (UN), this practice is part of the Clean Development Mechanism (CDM) and highlights the contribution of the projects to reduce greenhouse gas emissions and control global warming.

texto: A good relationship with the community in the region where a new Alupar project will be implemented also depends on respect for its past history. Before starting the works, an archeological team studies the records and documents related to the region’s ancestors. After this preliminary study, the team goes to the field with the appropriate tools and thoroughly searches the project’s area of influence. If an archaeological site is found, the archaeologists begin a process of recovery, preventing any potential damages caused by the project’s implementation and deepening their knowledge about the people who lived in the region. The archeological remains are analyzed and prepared to complement collections of the period. The work is followed by IPHAN, the Institute for National Historic and Artistic Heritage, and is also part of the environmental licensing process. Analysis Archaeological diagnosis and prospection Archaeological survey Excavations conducted by specialized teams Heritage Recovery of archaeological remains History A community with deeper knowledge on its own past More education and culture Alupar supports Programa Expedição (Expedition program), which is part of Vaga Lume, a non-profit association focused on educational, cultural and environmental projects. The initiative provides access to books and promotes reading habits among residents of communities located in the Legal Brazilian Amazon. The program consists of three actions: donation of the physical space where the community library will operate, training of volunteers who will mediate the reading, and encouraging the community for managing its own library. The project also encourages residents to produce handmade books, as a means to value the local culture. Participants register themselves and then provide illustrations to the story, thus contributing to the library’s collection. This is one of the many programs maintained by Alupar in this area. The Company also sponsors the musical education project of Fundação Bachiana Filarmônica (Bachiana Philharmonic Foundation), developed in association with conductor João Carlos Martins in the Paraisópolis community, located in the city of São Paulo. In addition, communities in the states of Pará, Maranhão and Minas Gerais participated in the project Mestres do Futuro, a project that recovers crafting techniques on the brink of extinction. Under this program, craftsmen are trained to impart their knowledge to youth groups in the community. In exchange, they receive not only income, but also respect for their work. In many municipalities where Alupar operates, the population attended a free theater play whose content is based on the region’s cultural characteristics, with environmental issues as background. The program, which is called Arte na Comunidade (Art in the community), invites local theater companies to perform the play and travel around many cities, under the arena theater model (a circular stage with seating surrounding it), so as to reach the largest possible audience. The play’s content also becomes a game which is then distributed to the local schools, raising awareness of students about environmental issues. These programs are developed through tax incentive under the Rouanet Law. Expedição Vaga Lume Promotes access to books and reading habits Bachiana Foundation Support to musical educational program Arte na Comunidade Travelling theatre that features plays based on environmental issues More sports Adjacent to the Verdescola Institute, located in the city of São Sebastião, state of São Paulo, is Verdesporte, a sports center supported by Alupar. Social and educational projects, including income generation and professional training programs, are also developed at the center. Additionally, the Company helps maintain a multi-purpose sports court located in the city Belo Horizonte, state of Minas Gerais. Athletes can also count on Alupar’s support. The Company sponsors the Brazilian Rugby Confederation, aiming to promote the sport in Brazil. At the Ferreira Gomes Hydropower Plant, the Jiu-Jitsu na Escola (Ju-Jitsu at school) project, developed through a partnership between Alupar and the city’s Secretary of Sports, aims to diminish the possibility of dropping out in school. Students with regular school attendance and good grades are invited to join the Ju-Jitsu team. Rugby Alupar sponsors the Brazilian Rugby Confederation to strengthen the sport in Brazil Jiu-Jitsu na Escola Construction of multi-purpose sports centers More health In addition to caring for the health of the communities where it operates by supporting vaccination and disease prevention campaigns, Alupar aids several health institutions, including APAE (an organization that offers health services for children and adults with special needs) and AACD (Assistance Association for Disabled Children). Health Vaccination and disease prevention campaigns APAE and AACD Funds donated to these institutions located across Brazil’s many states Butantã Institute Telemedicine to provide antivenom treatment in the Amazon region Respect for the local community Respect for the past history and opinion of the local communities is essential during each stage of implementation and operation of a project. For this reason, Alupar maintains an open communication channel through Social Communication Programs which are essential to information exchange between the Company and the community, so that everyone is aware of the most important events related to Alupar’s projects, ensuring transparency in any news of public interest. The project must be beneficial to all parties involved—based on this premise and the specific needs of each region, Alupar invests in programs to actively help improve quality of life in the local communities. Besides developing projects geared towards key topics, such as health and education, the Company offers strategic support and financial aid to vaccination campaigns and the expansion of health centers and schools. Through tax incentive laws, the community also benefits from cultural programs, including travelling theatre and maintenance of community libraries and multi-purpose sports centers. Communications Channel to maintain an open dialogue between the Company, the government and the community Revitalization Restoration of historic heritage buildings Investment Over 20 million reais invested in projects across Brazil Environmental Responsibility Economic growth and energy availability walk together. Consequently, the construction of hydropower plants and transmission lines are beneficial and essential to Brazil’s development. The gains from implementing such projects outweigh their potential negative impacts. Some of these benefits are low cost for energy generation, obtaining energy from a renewable sustainable source and developing programs that are important to preserve the environment in the region, creating new jobs and strengthening the local economy. Aligned with its commitment to the sustainable development of the communities where it operates, all Alupar projects are in compliance with the environmental laws based on the instruments and rites of the process of environmental licensing, and follow the resolutions of the National Environment Council (CONAMA). Each project has unique characteristics that are respected and taken into account during the Environmental Impact Study (EIA), so as to establish the most effective plan of action for each location. Based on this analysis, the Company develops programs for the preservation and recovery of Environmental Protection Areas, maintenance of the biodiversity of the fauna and flora, replacement and recovery of the native forests, maintenance of the quality of the water bodies, as well as other environmental compensations reverted to the maintenance of Conservation Units. These initiatives that aim to mitigate each project’ impacts are described in detail in the Basic Environmental Plan (PBA). Another initiative that contributes to the sustainability of Alupar’s energy generation projects is the certification to generate carbon credits which are traded on the international market. Created by the United Nations (UN), this practice is part of the Clean Development Mechanism (CDM) and highlights the contribution of the projects to reduce greenhouse gas emissions and control global warming. Fauna and Flora Maintenance of biodiversity Environment Replacement and recovery of native forests Water Maintenance of the quality of the water bodies Sustainability Because these are renewable energy sources, the water and the wind are sustainable alternatives when it comes to energy generation in Brazil. In addition, managing the environmental and social impacts is paramount in all stages of Alupar’s energy generation process, ensuring the community’s economic and social development. Regime fio d’água (hydropower plant without a reservoir) Lower impact on the surrounding area Wind Farm Compatible with other uses of the land

The work is followed by IPHAN, the Institute for National Historic and Artistic Heritage, and is also part of the environmental licensing process.

Analysis

  • Archaeological diagnosis and prospection

Archaeological survey

  • Excavations conducted by specialized teams

Heritage

  • Recovery of archaeological remains

History

  • A community with deeper knowledge on its own past

More education and culture

Alupar supports Programa Expedição (Expedition program), which is part of Vaga Lume, a non-profit association focused on educational, cultural and environmental projects. The initiative provides access to books and promotes reading habits among residents of communities located in the Legal Brazilian Amazon. The program consists of three actions: donation of the physical space where the community library will operate, training of volunteers who will mediate the reading, and encouraging the community for managing its own library. The project also encourages residents to produce handmade books, as a means to value the local culture. Participants register themselves and then provide illustrations to the story, thus contributing to the library’s collection.

This is one of the many programs maintained by Alupar in this area. The Company also sponsors the musical education project of Fundação Bachiana Filarmônica (Bachiana Philharmonic Foundation), developed in association with conductor João Carlos Martins in the Paraisópolis community, located in the city of São Paulo. In addition, communities in the states of Pará, Maranhão and Minas Gerais participated in the project Mestres do Futuro, a project that recovers crafting techniques on the brink of extinction. Under this program, craftsmen are trained to impart their knowledge to youth groups in the community. In exchange, they receive not only income, but also respect for their work.

In many municipalities where Alupar operates, the population attended a free theater play whose content is based on the region’s cultural characteristics, with environmental issues as background. The program, which is called Arte na Comunidade (Art in the community), invites local theater companies to perform the play and travel around many cities, under the arena theater model (a circular stage with seating surrounding it), so as to reach the largest possible audience. The play’s content also becomes a game which is then distributed to the local schools, raising awareness of students about environmental issues. These programs are developed through tax incentive under the Rouanet Law.

Expedição Vaga Lume

  • Promotes access to books and reading habits

Bachiana Foundation

  • Support to musical educational program

Arte na Comunidade

  • Travelling theatre that features plays based on environmental issues

More sports

Adjacent to the Verdescola Institute, located in the city of São Sebastião, state of São Paulo, is Verdesporte, a sports center supported by Alupar. Social and educational projects, including income generation and professional training programs, are also developed at the center. Additionally, the Company helps maintain a multi-purpose sports court located in the city Belo Horizonte, state of Minas Gerais. Athletes can also count on Alupar’s support. The Company sponsors the Brazilian Rugby Confederation, aiming to promote the sport in Brazil. At the Ferreira Gomes Hydropower Plant,  the Jiu-Jitsu na Escola (Ju-Jitsu at school) project, developed through a partnership between Alupar and the city’s Secretary of Sports, aims to diminish the possibility of dropping out in school. Students with regular school attendance and good grades are invited to join the Ju-Jitsu team.

Rugby

  • Alupar sponsors the Brazilian Rugby Confederation to strengthen the sport in Brazil

Jiu-Jitsu na Escola

  • Construction of multi-purpose sports centers

More health

In addition to caring for the health of the communities where it operates by supporting vaccination and disease prevention campaigns, Alupar aids several health institutions, including APAE (an organization that offers health services for children and adults with special needs) and AACD (Assistance Association for Disabled Children).

Health

  • Vaccination and disease prevention campaigns

APAE and AACD

  • Funds donated to these institutions located across Brazil’s many states

Butantã Institute

  • Telemedicine to provide antivenom treatment in the Amazon region

Respect for the local community

Respect for the past history and opinion of the local communities is essential during each stage of implementation and operation of a project. For this reason, Alupar maintains an open communication channel through Social Communication Programs which are essential to information exchange between the Company and the community, so that everyone is aware of the most important events related to Alupar’s projects, ensuring transparency in any news of public interest.

The project must be beneficial to all parties involved—based on this premise and the specific needs of each region, Alupar invests in programs to actively help improve quality of life in the local communities. Besides developing projects geared towards key topics, such as health and education, the Company offers strategic support and financial aid to vaccination campaigns and the expansion of health centers and schools. Through tax incentive laws, the community also benefits from cultural programs, including travelling theatre and maintenance of community libraries and multi-purpose sports centers.

Communications

  • Channel to maintain an open dialogue between the Company, the government and the community

Revitalization

  • Restoration of historic heritage buildings

Investment

  • Over 20 million reais invested in projects across Brazil

Environmental Responsibility

Economic growth and energy availability walk together. Consequently, the construction of hydropower plants and transmission lines are beneficial and essential to Brazil’s development. The gains from implementing such projects outweigh their potential negative impacts. Some of these benefits are low cost for energy generation, obtaining energy from a renewable sustainable source and developing programs that are important to preserve the environment in the region, creating new jobs and strengthening the local economy.

Aligned with its commitment to the sustainable development of the communities where it operates, all Alupar projects are in compliance with the environmental laws based on the instruments and rites of the process of environmental licensing, and follow the resolutions of the National Environment Council (CONAMA). Each project has unique characteristics that are respected and taken into account during the Environmental Impact Study (EIA), so as to establish the most effective plan of action for each location.

Based on this analysis, the Company develops programs for the preservation and recovery of Environmental Protection Areas, maintenance of the biodiversity of the fauna and flora, replacement and recovery of the native forests, maintenance of the quality of the water bodies, as well as other environmental compensations reverted to the maintenance of Conservation Units. These initiatives that aim to mitigate each project’ impacts are described in detail in the Basic Environmental Plan (PBA).

Another initiative that contributes to the sustainability of Alupar’s energy generation projects is the certification to generate carbon credits which are traded on the international market. Created by the United Nations (UN), this practice is part of the Clean Development Mechanism (CDM) and highlights the contribution of the projects to reduce greenhouse gas emissions and control global warming.

Fauna and Flora

  • Maintenance of biodiversity

Environment

  • Replacement and recovery of native forests

Water

  • Maintenance of the quality of the water bodies

Sustainability

Because these are renewable energy sources, the water and the wind are sustainable alternatives when it comes to energy generation in Brazil. In addition, managing the environmental and social impacts is paramount in all stages of Alupar’s energy generation process, ensuring the community’s economic and social development.

Regime fio d’água (hydropower plant without a reservoir)

  • Lower impact on the surrounding area

Wind Farm

  • Compatible with other uses of the land

titulo: Alupar and Furnas will build ten wind farms in Ceará
texto: Alupar and Furnas will build ten wind farms in Ceará The Consortium formed by Alupar Investimento S.A. (51%) and Furnas (49%) has sold at today‘s generation auction (ANEEL 07/2011), 204 MW of wind power for delivery from January 2016. The winning price was equivalent to R$ 110.00 MW/h, a discount of about 5% of the original. The companies will jointly build ten wind farms in the city of Aracati, Ceará, with investments of about R$ 800 million. “Alupar has been working on developing wind farms in order to strengthen the renewable energy sources of the Group and the partnership with Furnas was instrumental in the success of this auction,” said Enio Nucci, director of New Business from Alupar. “We are investing over R$ 1 billion in wind generation and we have a lot of interest in evaluating new opportunities. This victory established the partnership with Alupar and continues the policy of Furnas to diversify their ways of generating clean energy, “says Olga Simbalista, Director of Planning, Management and Business Interests of Furnas. Alupar and Furnas selected projects for wind turbines manufactured by the German Fuhrländer. The devices have 2.5 MW of power, height of 141 meters – the highest in Brazil, where the winds are less susceptible to interference, and trellis towers that do not compromise the dynamics of the turbine, rather than the more common tubular structures in the market. About Alupar Alupar diversified its sources of energy generation by investing in small and medium hydropower and SHPPs. The Company currently owns 459 MW of installed capacity, 179.4 MW being deployed and another 280 MW are under development. The Company‘s power generation projects are divided into three hydroelectric plants, the HPP São José (51 MW), in Rio Grande do Sul, HPP Foz do Rio Claro (68.4 MW), in Goiás, and HPP Ferreira Gomes (252 MW), at Amapá, and five small hydroelectric plants, the SHPP Queluz (30 MW) and SHPP Lavrinhas (30 MW) located in São Paulo, and the SHPPs Guática I (4 MW), Guática II (8 MW ) and Morro Azul (16 MW), located in Colombia. In the transmission sector, Alupar holds the concession of 19 transmission systems, with 715 km of lines under development in the North, in the states of Amazonas and Roraima, and other 4,750 km of lines operating located in the North and Northeast in the states of Pará, Maranhão, Piauí and Ceará, in the South, in the state of Santa Catarina, in the Southeast, in the states of Minas Gerais and Espírito Santo and in the Midwest region in the state of Mato Grosso. About Furnas Furnas has a complex of enterprises accounted for nearly 10% of generation in Brazil. There are 15 hydroelectric plants, two thermal plants, approximately 20,000 km of transmission lines and 52 substations. Of all energy consumed in the country, more than 40% pass by Furnas System. Currently, Furnas is building in partnership with business groups, wind farms Miassaba III and Rei dos Ventos I and III, which will begin operations in early 2012. In 2014 it will be the parks Famosa I, Rosada, Pau Brasil and São Paulo, whose buildings were secured through the sale of energy in the LER Auction 03/2011. Concentrated in the Northeast, the seven projects totaling 487.6 MW/h of installed capacity, power to 1.2 million people. In the expansion of Furnas is also the construction of three hydroelectric power plants – Santo Antonio (RO), Simplício (RJ / MG) and Batalha (GO / MG) – 26 new transmission lines and 14 substations, being erected with own resources and together with the private sector. In addition, the company also participates with 49% of HPP Teles Pires (MT / BP), topped in late 2010 in partnership with Neoenergia and in phase of feasibility studies.

titulo: Alupar conquista lote D no leilão da Aneel (Portuguese Only)
texto: Alupar conquista lote D no leilão da Aneel (Portuguese Only) No leilão de Linhas de Transmissão que a Aneel (Agência Nacional de Energia Elétrica) realizou nesta sexta-feira (27/11/2009), a Alupar saiu vitoriosa no lote D. O leilão foi realizado na sede da Bolsa de Valores do Rio de Janeiro. O consórcio Alupar Bimetal, formado pela Alupar Investimento S/A (60%) e Bimetal Indústria Metalúrgica Ltda (40%) venceu o leilão do lote D, aplicando um deságio de 12,03%. Isso significa uma Receita Anual Permitida (RAP) de R$ 8,4 milhões. O lote D, situado no Estado de Mato Grosso, é composto de uma linha de transmissão de cerca de 235 quilômetros de extensão e tensão de 230 kV. A previsão é que a LT entre em operação dentro de 20 meses, a partir da data de assinatura do contrato de concessão. (Portuguese Only)

titulo: Alupar launched power transmission system in MT
texto: Alupar launched power transmission system in MT Alupar launched on Friday (16), in the state of Mato Grosso, the transmission system Nova Mutum / Nobres / Cuiabá. Confirming Alupar‘s expertise in managing projects of this size, the stretch Nobres / Cuiabá was anticipated at four months and the stretch Nova Mutum / Nobres delivered three months in advance. With 235 km length, the transmission system was implemented by the Empresa de Transmissão de Energia do Mato Grosso S.A., a company formed by Alupar (60%) and Bimetal (40%). With this venture completed, Alupar now owns 4,950 kilometers of transmission lines in full operation, with 1,358 km only in the state of Mato Grosso. Other 715 km of transmission lines are being deployed in the northern region of Brazil. The system Nova Mutum / Nobres / Cuiabá belongs to the National Interlinked System (SIN), which will divert the surplus power generated in the state of Mato Grosso and serve the metropolitan region of Cuiabá.

titulo: Alupar vence leilão da Aneel para construir subestação em MT (Portuguese Only)
texto: Alupar vence leilão da Aneel para construir subestação em MT (Portuguese Only) A Alupar Investimento S/A arrematou na manhã desta sexta-feira (11/6) o lote F do leilão de Linhas de Transmissão promovido pela Agência Nacional de Energia Elétrica (Aneel). Com isso, a empresa ficará responsável pela construção de uma subestação de energia no Mato Grosso. A vitória consolida a atuação da Alupar no setor de transmissão, onde a Companhia passa a deter 18 transmissoras, e no próprio estado do Mato Grosso, onde a companhia já é responsável por outros três empreendimentos de transmissão. O lote foi bastante disputado e a Alupar saiu vencedora ao oferecer uma receita anual de R$ 2,96 milhões – deságio de 13,22% em relação ao valor inicial do leilão. A subestação de Várzea Grande, em 230/138 kv, ajudará a melhorar o sistema de distribuição de energia em toda a região metropolitana de Cuiabá e no sul mato-grossense. A partir da assinatura do contrato, a Alupar terá 24 meses para concluir a obra. (Portuguese Only)

titulo: Alupar vence leilão do lote D da Aneel
texto: Alupar vence leilão do lote D da Aneel Na última sexta-feira, 27 de junho, a Alupar, holding que atua na área de geração e transmissão de energia, através do consórcio TBE Centro-Oeste, ganhou o leilão da Aneel (Agência Nacional de Energia Elétrica) para o lote D, no Mato Grosso, passando pelos municípios de Juína, Brasnorte, Sapezal, Nova Mutum, Sorriso, Sinop, Tangará da Serra, Campo Novo dos Parecis, Lucas do Rio Verde e Vera. O consórcio TBE Centro-Oeste, formado pela EATE (51%), empresa controlada pelo grupo Alupar, e pela Cemig (49%), venceu o consórcio formado pela Neoenergia e pela Odebrecht, aplicando um deságio de 29,5%. Isso significa uma Receita Anual Permitida (RAP) de R$ 25,95 milhões. O lote D, com aproximadamente 775 quilômetros de extensão e tensão de 230 kV tem previsão de construção de duas subestações, uma em Juína, outra em Parecis, que entrarão em operação em 2010. Além de ser um dos maiores lotes do leilão, também não apresenta riscos ambientais de outros lotes com extensão semelhante. Com esse leilão, a Alupar soma aproximadamente 4.400 quilômetros de transmissão de energia. Esse empreendimento gerará 2.700 empregos diretos e possibilitará o escoamento de energia elétrica dos diversos projetos de geração que se implantarão no estado do Mato Grosso. Desses projetos, 1.120 MW estão previstos para os próximos dois anos e contribuirão com o desenvolvimento do estado e para o aumento da capacidade nacional de geração de energia elétrica.

titulo: Alupar will invest in power generation in Colombia
texto: Alupar will invest in power generation in Colombia Alupar Investimento S/A assumed the Risaralda Energy SAS/ESP – a company that owns the rights and authorizations to develop a complex of small hydroelectric plants in the state of Risaralda, Colombia. The complex consists of three projects, totalizing approximately 30 megawatts of installed capacity. The investment will be around US$ 70 million, with construction planned for 24 months. The energy generated will be traded on the open market power in Colombia. The group decided to invest in Colombia due to the large growth potential of the country, with stable rules and solid regulations. Alupar expects to gradually increase investments in Colombian territory. With this new venture, Alupar expands its generating capacity by a further 30 MW, reaching a total of around 460 MW of installed capacity. The company also operates 5,665 kilometers of transmission lines, 200 kilometers in Chile. Therefore, Alupar expands its international presence and become one of the big energy groups in the electricity segment.
corpo:
Alupar will invest in power generation in Colombia

Alupar Investimento S/A assumed the Risaralda Energy SAS/ESP – a company that owns the rights and authorizations to develop a complex of small hydroelectric plants in the state of Risaralda, Colombia. The complex consists of three projects, totalizing approximately 30 megawatts of installed capacity.

The investment will be around US$ 70 million, with construction planned for 24 months.

The energy generated will be traded on the open market power in Colombia.

The group decided to invest in Colombia due to the large growth potential of the country, with stable rules and solid regulations. Alupar expects to gradually increase investments in Colombian territory.

With this new venture, Alupar expands its generating capacity by a further 30 MW, reaching a total of around 460 MW of installed capacity. The company also operates 5,665 kilometers of transmission lines, 200 kilometers in Chile. Therefore, Alupar expands its international presence and become one of the big energy groups in the electricity segment.

titulo: Alupar wins auction to build a 715 km transmission line in the North of Brazil
texto: Alupar wins auction to build a 715 km transmission line in the North of Brazil Alupar Investimento S.A. won the lot A in the ANEEL nº 004/2011 today’s auction, to build a 715 Km transmission line in the North of Brazil. The foreseen investment is R$ 969.257.670,00, with an Allowed Annual Revenue (RAP) of R$ 121.128.000,00, with no discounts if compared with the original RAP established by ANEEL. Lot A is composed by a double circuit transmission line and three substations in Amazonas (Lechuga Substation) and Roraima (Equador and Boa Vista Substations). This project will connect the city of Boa Vista (RR) to the National Interconnected System (SIN) and will allow the reduction of expenses with the Fuel Consumption Account (CCC) and the energy imports from Venezuela. Boa Vista Consortium is formed by Alupar (51%) and Centrais Elétricas do Norte do Brasil S.A. – Eletronorte (49%). With the victory in this new auction, Alupar will add 715 km of transmission lines to its current portfolio of 5,000 km of lines executed by the company in Brazil and Chile.

texto: Alupar wins Lot D in transmission auction Alupar won on Friday (16), in an auction of transmission lines performed by the National Agency of Electrical Energy (ANEEL) the Lot D, composed by the substations Abdon Batista (525 kV) and Gaspar (230 kV), both in the state of Santa Catarina. The venture will be performed by Empresa Catarinense de Transmissão de Energia S.A., a company formed by Alupar (42.5%), Celesc (30.9%), Cemig (19.1%) and MDU (7.5%). With a planned investment of R$ 191 million, the project will generate about 950 direct jobs during the 24 months specified by ANEEL for the construction, from the signing of the concession contract. The system aims to meet the integration of the hydroelectric power plants of Garibaldi (175 MW) and São Roque (214 MW) to the National Interlinked System, as well as forecasting the integration of some SHPPs (Small Hydro Power Plants) to request access to the Celesc distribution system. In addition, the venture will serve to expand the supply of electricity to the region of Vale do Itajai and to the Blumenau substation (230/138 kV). Alupar, which already operates 500 km of transmission lines and two substations in the state of Santa Catarina, will have two new substations in the state. With this new venture, Alupar consolidates a group of 20 power transmission companies with 5,665 km of lines and 14 substations own.
corpo:
Alupar wins Lot D in transmission auction

Alupar won on Friday (16), in an auction of transmission lines performed by the National Agency of Electrical Energy (ANEEL) the Lot D, composed by the substations Abdon Batista (525 kV) and Gaspar (230 kV), both in the state of Santa Catarina. The venture will be performed by Empresa Catarinense de Transmissão de Energia S.A., a company formed by Alupar (42.5%), Celesc (30.9%), Cemig (19.1%) and MDU (7.5%).

With a planned investment of R$ 191 million, the project will generate about 950 direct jobs during the 24 months specified by ANEEL for the construction, from the signing of the concession contract.

The system aims to meet the integration of the hydroelectric power plants of Garibaldi (175 MW) and São Roque (214 MW) to the National Interlinked System, as well as forecasting the integration of some SHPPs (Small Hydro Power Plants) to request access to the Celesc distribution system. In addition, the venture will serve to expand the supply of electricity to the region of Vale do Itajai and to the Blumenau substation (230/138 kV).

Alupar, which already operates 500 km of transmission lines and two substations in the state of Santa Catarina, will have two new substations in the state.

With this new venture, Alupar consolidates a group of 20 power transmission companies with 5,665 km of lines and 14 substations own.

titulo: Commercial Operation of Authorized Enhancement of ERTE
texto: Commercial Operation of Authorized Enhancement of ERTE On June 24th 2012, the authorized enhancement of the “Empresa Regional de Transmissão de Energia S.A.” (ERTE) was energized and started its commercial operation. It consists of the Castanhal substation, in which it is installed a capacitor bank series in 230 kV, 151 Mvar, y 2.1 km of transmission lines. texto: EBTE Opening Alupar announces the startup of EBTE – Empresa Brasileira de Trasmissão de Energia S.A, consisting of the transmission lines, Juína-Maggi, double circuit, with 215 km length, connecting new Juína substation to Maggi substation; transmission line Maggi-Juba, double circuit, with 232 km length, starting in Maggi substation and ending in Juba substation; transmission line Maggi-Parecis, double circuit, with 106 km length, starting in Maggi substation and ending in the new Parecis substation and the transmission line Nova Mutum-Sorriso-Sinop, simple circuit, with 222 km length, linking the substations of Nova Mutum, Sorriso and Sinop. The project belongs to EATE (51%), a subsidiary of Alupar, and CEMIG (49%). With the startup of this new line, Alupar Group has 14 operating companies, totaling 4,366.5 km long, and 4 more transmission systems under construction, scheduled to be operational between 2011 and 2012. The work started in 2009 created jobs and development to the state of Mato Grosso.

The project belongs to EATE (51%), a subsidiary of Alupar, and CEMIG (49%).

With the startup of this new line, Alupar Group has 14 operating companies, totaling 4,366.5 km long, and 4 more transmission systems under construction, scheduled to be operational between 2011 and 2012.

titulo: Foz do Rio Claro HPP – 2nd turbine’s startup
texto: Foz do Rio Claro HPP – 2nd turbine’s startup Alupar Investimento received, as published in the Federal official Gazette, on December 2, 2010, the official authorization from the National Electric Power Agency (Aneel) to start the commercial operation of the second 34.2MW power generating unit of the “Engenheiro José Luiz Müller de Godoy Pereira” HPP. Located between the cities of Caçu and São Simão, in southern Goiás, the hydroelectric power plant, has capacity for 68.4 MW, divided in two turbines and power assured of 41 MW. The “Engenheiro José Luiz Müller de Godoy Pereira” HPP belongs to Alupar Investimento S/A (50.1%) in partnership with FI-FGTS (49.9%).
corpo:
Foz do Rio Claro HPP – 2nd turbine’s startup

Alupar Investimento received, as published in the Federal official Gazette, on December 2, 2010, the official authorization from the National Electric Power Agency (Aneel) to start the commercial operation of the second 34.2MW power generating unit of the “Engenheiro José Luiz Müller de Godoy Pereira” HPP.

Located between the cities of Caçu and São Simão, in southern Goiás, the hydroelectric power plant, has capacity for 68.4 MW, divided in two turbines and power assured of 41 MW.

The “Engenheiro José Luiz Müller de Godoy Pereira” HPP belongs to Alupar Investimento S/A (50.1%) in partnership with FI-FGTS (49.9%).

titulo: Foz do Rio Claro HPP launched in Goiás
texto: Foz do Rio Claro HPP launched in Goiás Foz do Rio Claro Hydroelectric Power Plant launched on Tuesday, October 19, in Goiás. The plant, with installed capacity of 68.4 MW and 41 MW of assured power, belongs to Alupar Investimento S/A (50.1%) in partnership with FI-FGTS (49.9%). The undertaking counts on two turbines of 34.2 MW and a reservoir with 7.7 km². The work started in August 2007, and generated job positions and development to the cities of Caçu and São Simão, in southern Goiás. The undertaking was officially named Engenheiro José Luiz Müller de Godoy Pereira.
corpo:
Foz do Rio Claro HPP launched in Goiás

The undertaking counts on two turbines of 34.2 MW and a reservoir with 7.7 km².

The work started in August 2007, and generated job positions and development to the cities of Caçu and São Simão, in southern Goiás.

texto: Groundbreaking for UHE Ferreira Gomes is celebrated Last Wednesday, September 28th, the office of Ferreira Gomes Energia for the construction of the Ferreira Gomes Hydropower Plant, in the State of Amapá, was inaugurated. On the previous day, State government officials and representatives from Ferreira Gomes Energia signed the license for implementing the worksite and the area loaned for the power plant construction. With installed capacity of 252 [MW], generating a sufficient volume to supply a city with over 500,000 people, the Ferreira Gomes Hydropower Plant will be built by the company Ferreira Gomes Energia S/A, a member of the holding Alupar Investimento. Currently, a considerable part of the energy that supplies Amapá is generated from the diesel oil consumption, a non-renewable source of energy. With installed capacity of 252 [MW], generating a sufficient volume to supply a city with over 500,000 people, the Ferreira Gomes Hydropower Plant will be built by the company Ferreira Gomes Energia S/A, a member of the holding Alupar Investimento.

The construction works for the Ferreira Gomes Hydropower Plant shall start in October.

titulo: Material Fact – Acquisition of La Virgen
texto: Material Fact – Acquisition of La Virgen ALUPAR INVESTIMENTO S.A. (“Companhia” or “Alupar”) , a publicly-held company registered with the Brazilian Securities and Exchange Commission (“CVM”) under number 2149-0, pursuant to Article 157, paragraph four, of Law 6404, of December 15, 1976, as amended, and CVM Instruction 358 of January 3, 2002, as amended, hereby informs its shareholders and the market in general that, on this date, and as authorized by its Board of Directors, it acquired seven million, one hundred and seventy-six thousand (7,176,000) common shares issued by the Peruvian company La Virgen S.A.C., which represent sixty-five percent (65%) of the total and voting capital stock of said company, for the amount of three million, five hundred and twenty-five thousand dollars (US$3,525,000.00), held by Peruana de Energía S.A.A.. La Virgen S.A.C. holds, in compliance with Peru’s laws, the concession, for an undetermined period of time, of the project of the La Virgen hydroelectric power plant, with approximate capacity for sixty-four megawatts (64 MW), located in Chanchamayo, Perú, to be developed by means of the “Contrato de Concesión de Generación No. 253-2005, dated October 7, 2005, executed with the Ministry of Mines and Energy”, and the “Contrato de Concesión de Transmisión No. 313-2008, dated June 11, 2008, executed with the Ministry of Mines and Energy”. The project will include the 138 kV La Virgen – Caripa transmission line, with length of approximately 62.57 km, as well as the complementary electrical works for the connection: (i) in the new Electric Substation La Virgen 13.8/138 kV, and (ii) in the expansion of the Substation Caripa 138 kV. Total investments in this new project are estimated at approximately one hundred and five million dollars (US$105,000,000.00). To access the material fact, click here.

(“EATE”) of ten percent (10%) of the capital stock of the transmission companies Companhia Transleste de Transmissão S.A., Companhia Transirapé de Transmissão (direct subsidiaries of the Company) and Companhia Transudeste de Transmissão (affiliated of the Company), currently held by Orteng Equipamentos e Sistemas S.A. (“Orteng”). After closing the deal, the Company, which held a 28.71% indirect interest in the respective transmission companies, will hold a 33.71% indirect interest. In view of the acquisition, EATE will pay Orteng the base price of thirty-four million and one hundred thousand reais (BRL 34,100,000.00), restated by the SELIC rate as of December 31, 2012. Any payments from the respective transmission companies to Orteng as of December 31, 2012 will be discounted from the base price. These payments include the declaration and/or distribution and/or payment or dividends, declaration and/or payment of interest on equity, capital reduction, agreements with and/or payments to related parties, in addition to dividends for 2011 paid in 2013 and dividends for 2012 paid as of 2013, inclusive. The Share Purchase Agreement between EATE and Orteng was entered into on this date; the conclusion of the transaction and the consequent share acquisition are subject to conditions precedent, including: (i) prior and express authorization by the Brazilian Electricity Regulatory Agency – ANEEL; (ii) prior and express authorization by debt holders; (iii) prior and express authorization by Brazil’s antitrust authority – CADE. The Company will keep its shareholders and the market informed of the progress of the acquisition by its direct subsidiary EATE. For more information, click here.

texto: Material Fact – Acquisition of the capital stock of each of the companies of the Aracati Complex MATERIAL FACT ALUPAR INVESTIMENTO S.A. (“Company”), a publicly-held company, registered with the Brazilian Securities and Exchange Commission (CVM) under number 2149-0, in accordance with article 157, paragraph 4 of Law 6404, of December 15, 1976, as amended, and CVM Instruction 358, of January 3, 2002, as amended, hereby informs its shareholders and the market in general that it concluded today the acquisition of the capital stock of each of the companies of the Aracati Complex, as follows: seven million, three hundred fifteen thousand and seven hundred (7,315,700) shares related to Energia dos Ventos I, four million, four hundred and fifty-nine thousand (4,459,000) shares related to Energia dos Ventos II, six million, five hundred ninety-five thousand and four hundred (6,595,400) shares related to Energia dos Ventos III, nine million, six hundred and four thousand (9,604,000) shares related to Energia dos Ventos IV and five million, eight hundred sixty-five thousand and three hundred (5,865,300) shares related to Energia dos Ventos X, totaling thirty-three million, eight hundred thirty-nine thousand and four hundred (33,839,400) registered, book-entry common shares with no par value, equivalent to forty-nine percent (49.00%) of the Aracati Complex. titulo: Minutes of the Annual and Extraordinary Shareholders´ Meeting
texto: Minutes of the Annual and Extraordinary Shareholders´ Meeting Minutes of the Annual and Extraordinary Shareholders´ Meeting Held on April 16, 2014 Minutes drawn up in summary format 1. DATE, TIME AND VENUE: April 16, 2014, at 3:00 p.m., at the auditorium located in the 3rd floor of the Company’s headquarters at Avenida Dr. Cardoso de Melo, nº 1855, Bloco I, in the city and state of São Paulo. 2. CALL NOTICE: Call notice was published in the Diário Oficial do Estado de São Paulo on April 1, 2 and 3, 2014, on pages 99, 46 and 73, respectively, and in the Valor Econômico newspaper, on April 1, 2 and 3, 2014, on pages E2, E3 and E6, respectively. 3. PUBLICATIONS: The Company published the Notice to Shareholders to which Article 133 of Law 6,404/76 refers in the Diário Oficial do Estado de São Paulo on February 28, 2014, March 1 and 2, 2014, on pages 401, 40 and 27, respectively, and in the Valor Econômico newspaper on February 28, 2014, March 5 and 6, 2014, on pages E2, E2 e B8, respectively. The Company’s Financial Statements related to the fiscal year ended December 31, 2013, accompanied by the Management Report and the Independent Auditors’ Opinion were published in the Diário Oficial do Estado de São Paulo (pages 5 to 30) and in the Valor Econômico newspaper (pages E10 to E23) on March 11, 2014. 4. ATTENDANCE: On first call, the meeting was attended by shareholders representing approximately 93.43% of the voting capital stock, as per the signatures in the Shareholders Attendance List of the Company. Additionally, the representative of the Company’s independent auditors, Luiz Carlos Passetti, and the Company’s executive officer, Marcelo Patrício Fernandes Costa, also attended the meeting, pursuant to Article 134, paragraph 1 of Law 6,404/76. 5. PRESIDING: Chairman: José Luiz de Godoy Pereira; Secretary: Helio Carlos Ferreira Filho, attorney-in-fact of Guarupart Participações Ltda. 6. AGENDA: At the Annual Shareholders’ Meeting: (a) To analyze the management’s accounts, examine, discuss and vote on the Company’s Financial Statements related to the fiscal year ended December 31, 2013, accompanied by the Management Report and the Independent Auditors’ Opinion; (b) To resolve on the allocation of net income for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2013 and the distribution of dividends; (c) To acknowledge and formalize the resignation of José Lazaro Alves Rodrigues, sitting member of the Board of Directors, and Cesar Luiz de Godoy Pereira, alternate member of the Board of Directors, and to elect Marcelo Tosto de Oliveira Carvalho sitting member of the Board of Directors. At the Extraordinary Shareholders’ Meeting: (d) To establish the annual overall compensation of the Company’s Management for fiscal year 2014; (e) To rectify and ratify the amounts of the annual overall compensation of the Company’s Management for fiscal year 2013. 7. RESOLUTIONS: At the Annual Shareholders’ Meeting: The attending shareholders approved, by majority vote, with abstentions recorded, the drawing up of these minutes in summary format, as well as its publication with omission of the attending shareholders’ signatures, as permitted by Article 130, paragraphs 1 and 2, of Law 6,404/76; (a) The attending shareholders approved, by majority vote, with abstentions recorded, the Company’s Financial Statements related to the fiscal year ended December 31, 2013, accompanied by the Management Report and the Independent Auditors’ Opinion, as published in the Diário Oficial do Estado de São Paulo (pages 5 to 30) and in the Valor Econômico newspaper (pages E10 to E23) on March 11, 2014. (b) The attending shareholders approved, by unanimous vote, with abstentions recorded, the allocation of net income for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2013, in the amount of R$289,851,246.80, as follows: (i) Allocation of 5% the net income, in the amount of R$14,492,562.34, to Legal Reserve, which will total R$58,151,832.69; (ii) Distribution of dividends to shareholders totaling R$193,719,558.00 (R$0.31 per common share issued by the Company, R$0.31 per preferred share issued by the Company and R$0.93 per Unit of the Company), of which (i) R$137,679,342.23 will be distributed as minimum mandatory dividends of 50% of the adjusted net income for the year, in compliance with Article 36 of the Company’s Bylaws, and (ii) R$56,040,215.77 will be distributed as supplementary dividends; (iii) Allocation of R$81,639,126.46 to Investment Reserve, which will total R$642,587,793.64; and (iv) Ratification of the interim dividends to be paid from the existing profit reserve account in the balance sheet of December 31, 2012, pursuant to Article 37 of the Company’s Bylaws, approved by the Board of Directors on February 27, 2014, totaling R$156,225,450.00 (R$0.25 per common share issued by the Company, R$0.25 per preferred share issued by the Company, and R$0.75 per Unit of the Company). The payment of dividends declared herein and of interim dividends herein ratified will be made on May 2, 2014 to shareholders inscribed in the Company’s records at the end of April 16, 2014, as per the caput of Article 205 of the Brazilian Corporation Law. Accordingly, Company shares will be traded ex-dividend as of April 17, 2014. (c) The shareholders accepted the resignation of José Lazaro Alves Rodrigues, sitting member of the Board of Directors, and Cesar Luiz de Godoy Pereira, alternate member of the Board of Directors, who submitted their resignation by letter dated March 11, 2014. Furthermore, the attending shareholders approved, by majority vote, with abstentions recorded, the election of Marcelo Tosto de Oliveira Carvalho, Brazilian, married, business administrator, bearer of identity document (RG) number 6.191.720-5 SSP-RJ, inscribed in the roll of individual taxpayers (CPF/MF) under number 007.274.888-56, resident and domiciled in the city and state of São Paulo, with office at Avenida Doutor Cardoso de Melo, 1855, Bloco I, 9º andar, Vila Olímpia, CEP 04548-005, in the city and state of São Paulo, for the position of sitting member of the Board of Directors, to replace José Lazaro Alves Rodrigues and finish the current term, i.e. with term of office running through the Annual Shareholders’ Meeting that will approve the accounts of fiscal year 2014. Marcelo Tosto de Oliveira Carvalho will take office as sitting member of the Board of Directors upon signing the Instrument of Investiture, drawn up in the Company’s records, and his investiture will be conditioned to the previous subscription to the Management’s Statement of Agreement, pursuant to the Level 2 regulations of BM&FBOVESPA S.A. – Securities, Commodities and Futures Exchange. At the Extraordinary Shareholders’ Meeting: (d) The attending shareholders approved, by majority vote, with abstentions recorded, the annual overall compensation of the Company’s Management for fiscal year 2014 (January 1, 2014 to December 31, 2014) in the amount of up to R$12,930,000.00, of which R$1,570,000.00 referring to the compensation for the members of the Board of Directors, and R$11,360,000.00 referring to the compensation for the members of the Board of Executive Officers. (e) The attending shareholders approved, by majority vote, with abstentions recorded, the rectification of the annual overall compensation of the Company’s Management proposed for fiscal year 2013 and approved at the Annual Shareholders’ Meeting held on March 28, 2013, originally approved in the amount of up to R$9,400,000.00, of which R$1,283,000.00 referring to the compensation for the members of the Board of Directors, and R$8,117,000.00 referring to the compensation for the members of the Board of Executive Officers. The rectified amount is up to R$10,408,886.53, of which R$1,315,328.35 referring to the compensation for the members of the Board of Directors, and R$9,093,558.18 referring to the compensation for the members of the Board of Executive Officers, being hereby ratified as the annual overall compensation of the Company’s Management proposed for fiscal year 2013. 8. CLOSURE: There being no further business to discuss and in the absence of any other manifestation, the meeting was adjourned and these minutes were drawn up, which was then read, approved, and signed by the shareholders identified below and the presiding board of the Shareholders’ Meeting. São Paulo, April 16, 2014 This is a free translation of the original minutes filed in the Company’s records Helio Carlos Ferreira Filho Secretary To access the document, click here .

Minutes drawn up in summary format

1. DATE, TIME AND VENUE: April 16, 2014, at 3:00 p.m., at the auditorium located in the 3rd floor of the Company’s headquarters at Avenida Dr. Cardoso de Melo, nº 1855, Bloco I, in the city and state of São Paulo.

2. CALL NOTICE: Call notice was published in the Diário Oficial do Estado de São Paulo on April 1, 2 and 3, 2014, on pages 99, 46 and 73, respectively, and in the Valor Econômico newspaper, on April 1, 2 and 3, 2014, on pages E2, E3 and E6, respectively.

3. PUBLICATIONS: The Company published the Notice to Shareholders to which Article 133 of Law 6,404/76 refers in the Diário Oficial do Estado de São Paulo on February 28, 2014, March 1 and 2, 2014, on pages 401, 40 and 27, respectively, and in the Valor Econômico newspaper on February 28, 2014, March 5 and 6, 2014, on pages E2, E2 e B8, respectively. The Company’s Financial Statements related to the fiscal year ended December 31, 2013, accompanied by the Management Report and the Independent Auditors’ Opinion were published in the Diário Oficial do Estado de São Paulo (pages 5 to 30) and in the Valor Econômico newspaper (pages E10 to E23) on March 11, 2014.

4. ATTENDANCE: On first call, the meeting was attended by shareholders representing approximately 93.43% of the voting capital stock, as per the signatures in the Shareholders Attendance List of the Company. Additionally, the representative of the Company’s independent auditors, Luiz Carlos Passetti, and the Company’s executive officer, Marcelo Patrício Fernandes Costa, also attended the meeting, pursuant to Article 134, paragraph 1 of Law 6,404/76.

5. PRESIDING: Chairman: José Luiz de Godoy Pereira; Secretary: Helio Carlos Ferreira Filho, attorney-in-fact of Guarupart Participações Ltda.

6. AGENDA:

At the Annual Shareholders’ Meeting:

(a) To analyze the management’s accounts, examine, discuss and vote on the Company’s Financial Statements related to the fiscal year ended December 31, 2013, accompanied by the Management Report and the Independent Auditors’ Opinion;

(b) To resolve on the allocation of net income for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2013 and the distribution of dividends;

(c) To acknowledge and formalize the resignation of José Lazaro Alves Rodrigues, sitting member of the Board of Directors, and Cesar Luiz de Godoy Pereira, alternate member of the Board of Directors, and to elect Marcelo Tosto de Oliveira Carvalho sitting member of the Board of Directors.

At the Extraordinary Shareholders’ Meeting:

(d) To establish the annual overall compensation of the Company’s Management for fiscal year 2014;

(e) To rectify and ratify the amounts of the annual overall compensation of the Company’s Management for fiscal year 2013.

7. RESOLUTIONS:

At the Annual Shareholders’ Meeting:

The attending shareholders approved, by majority vote, with abstentions recorded, the drawing up of these minutes in summary format, as well as its publication with omission of the attending shareholders’ signatures, as permitted by Article 130, paragraphs 1 and 2, of Law 6,404/76;

(a) The attending shareholders approved, by majority vote, with abstentions recorded, the Company’s Financial Statements related to the fiscal year ended December 31, 2013, accompanied by the Management Report and the Independent Auditors’ Opinion, as published in the Diário Oficial do Estado de São Paulo (pages 5 to 30) and in the Valor Econômico newspaper (pages E10 to E23) on March 11, 2014.

(b) The attending shareholders approved, by unanimous vote, with abstentions recorded, the allocation of net income for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2013, in the amount of R$289,851,246.80, as follows:

(i) Allocation of 5% the net income, in the amount of R$14,492,562.34, to Legal Reserve, which will total R$58,151,832.69;

(ii) Distribution of dividends to shareholders totaling R$193,719,558.00 (R$0.31 per common share issued by the Company, R$0.31 per preferred share issued by the Company and R$0.93 per Unit of the Company), of which (i) R$137,679,342.23 will be distributed as minimum mandatory dividends of 50% of the adjusted net income for the year, in compliance with Article 36 of the Company’s Bylaws, and (ii) R$56,040,215.77 will be distributed as supplementary dividends;

(iii) Allocation of R$81,639,126.46 to Investment Reserve, which will total R$642,587,793.64; and

(iv) Ratification of the interim dividends to be paid from the existing profit reserve account in the balance sheet of December 31, 2012, pursuant to Article 37 of the Company’s Bylaws, approved by the Board of Directors on February 27, 2014, totaling R$156,225,450.00 (R$0.25 per common share issued by the Company, R$0.25 per preferred share issued by the Company, and R$0.75 per Unit of the Company).

The payment of dividends declared herein and of interim dividends herein ratified will be made on May 2, 2014 to shareholders inscribed in the Company’s records at the end of April 16, 2014, as per the caput of Article 205 of the Brazilian Corporation Law. Accordingly, Company shares will be traded ex-dividend as of April 17, 2014.

(c) The shareholders accepted the resignation of José Lazaro Alves Rodrigues, sitting member of the Board of Directors, and Cesar Luiz de Godoy Pereira, alternate member of the Board of Directors, who submitted their resignation by letter dated March 11, 2014.

Furthermore, the attending shareholders approved, by majority vote, with abstentions recorded, the election of Marcelo Tosto de Oliveira Carvalho, Brazilian, married, business administrator, bearer of identity document (RG) number 6.191.720-5 SSP-RJ, inscribed in the roll of individual taxpayers (CPF/MF) under number 007.274.888-56, resident and domiciled in the city and state of São Paulo, with office at Avenida Doutor Cardoso de Melo, 1855, Bloco I, 9º andar, Vila Olímpia, CEP 04548-005, in the city and state of São Paulo, for the position of sitting member of the Board of Directors, to replace José Lazaro Alves Rodrigues and finish the current term, i.e. with term of office running through the Annual Shareholders’ Meeting that will approve the accounts of fiscal year 2014.

Marcelo Tosto de Oliveira Carvalho will take office as sitting member of the Board of Directors upon signing the Instrument of Investiture, drawn up in the Company’s records, and his investiture will be conditioned to the previous subscription to the Management’s Statement of Agreement, pursuant to the Level 2 regulations of BM&FBOVESPA S.A. – Securities, Commodities and Futures Exchange.

At the Extraordinary Shareholders’ Meeting:

(d) The attending shareholders approved, by majority vote, with abstentions recorded, the annual overall compensation of the Company’s Management for fiscal year 2014 (January 1, 2014 to December 31, 2014) in the amount of up to R$12,930,000.00, of which R$1,570,000.00 referring to the compensation for the members of the Board of Directors, and R$11,360,000.00 referring to the compensation for the members of the Board of Executive Officers.

(e) The attending shareholders approved, by majority vote, with abstentions recorded, the rectification of the annual overall compensation of the Company’s Management proposed for fiscal year 2013 and approved at the Annual Shareholders’ Meeting held on March 28, 2013, originally approved in the amount of up to R$9,400,000.00, of which R$1,283,000.00 referring to the compensation for the members of the Board of Directors, and R$8,117,000.00 referring to the compensation for the members of the Board of Executive Officers. The rectified amount is up to R$10,408,886.53, of which R$1,315,328.35 referring to the compensation for the members of the Board of Directors, and R$9,093,558.18 referring to the compensation for the members of the Board of Executive Officers, being hereby ratified as the annual overall compensation of the Company’s Management proposed for fiscal year 2013.

8. CLOSURE: There being no further business to discuss and in the absence of any other manifestation, the meeting was adjourned and these minutes were drawn up, which was then read, approved, and signed by the shareholders identified below and the presiding board of the Shareholders’ Meeting.

São Paulo, April 16, 2014

This is a free translation of the original minutes filed in the Company’s records

Helio Carlos Ferreira Filho
Secretary

titulo: Notice to the Market – Annual Permitted Revenue (RAP) – Cycle of 2014
texto: Notice to the Market – Annual Permitted Revenue (RAP) – Cycle of 2014 Notice to the Market – Annual Permitted Revenue (RAP) – Cycle of 2014 ALUPAR INVESTIMENTO S.A. (“Company”), a publicly-held company registered with the CVM under no 21490, hereby informs its shareholders and the market in general that, in accordance with the Ratificatory Decision 1756/20143 of June 24, 20143, published in the Diário Oficial da União, ANEEL has established the Annual Permitted Revenue (RAP) and New Installations Basic Grid (RBNI) for power transmission concessionaires for the 2014/2015 cycle, effective as of July 1, 2014, which applies to all Alupar’s transmission companies. The transmission companies’ revenues will be restated in accordance with the indexes provided for in the respective concession agreements accrued in the last 12 months, i.e. 6.37% for agreements pegged to the IPCA consumer price index and 7.84% for agreements pegged to the IGP-M general market price index. The full version of the Ratificatory Decision 1756/2014 as well as Attachment I thereto can be accessed via the respective links below: http://www.aneel.gov.br/cedoc/reh20141756ti.pdf http://www.aneel.gov.br/cedoc/areh20141756_2.pdf São Paulo, July 1, 2014 To access the document, click here .

texto: Projetos devem atingir 730 megawatts Com o objetivo de minimizar a futura eventual escassez de oferta de energia elétrica no Brasil, prevista para 2014, a Alupar está investindo na expansão da geração de energia renovável por meio de Pequenas Centrais Hidrelétricas (PCHs). São 14 projetos em curso nas regiões Sul, Sudeste, Centro-Oeste e Nordeste do País. As prospecções tiveram início em janeiro de 2008 e alguns projetos já foram entregues à Aneel (Agência Nacional de Energia Elétrica) para aprovação. A Companhia planeja investir aproximadamente R$ 2 bilhões na construção das usinas hidrelétricas que forem identificadas a partir desses projetos. A expectativa é chegar a uma capacidade instalada de 730 Megawatts a partir de 2013. Além desses projetos, a Alupar já tem 2 PCHs e 2 UHEs em construção, cujas operações estão previstas para começar em 2010, num total de 180 Megawatts.

titulo: Signed the concession for the installation of Ferreira Gomes HPP
texto: Signed the concession for the installation of Ferreira Gomes HPP Mines and Energy Minister Márcio Zimmermann signed this Tuesday (11/09) a concession agreement to implant and deploy Ferreira Gomes hydroelectric power plant in Amapá state. The document has been signed also by the representatives of Ferreira Gomes Energia S.A., a company established by Alupar in order to execute this project. Ferreira Gomes HPP will be installed Araguari river in Ferreira Gomes county (state of Amapá). The hydroelectric power plant concession has been bought at auctions by Alupar in the first power supply auction A-5 in the current year, promoted on July 30th by Aneel, Brazilian Electricity Regulatory Agency. This undertaking evaluated in R$ 810 million is considered of essential importance for the energy supply in the North region that nowadays depends on thermal supplies (the most expensive and polluting resource). The hydroelectric power plant will have a power of 252 MW.

titulo: UHE São José é inaugurada em RS (Portuguese Only)
texto: UHE São José é inaugurada em RS (Portuguese Only) A hidrelétrica São José foi inaugurada nesta terça-feira, 29 de março, no estado do Rio Grande do Sul. A usina, com capacidade instalada de 51,0 MW e energia assegurada de 30,4 MW, pertence à Alupar Investimento S/A, que detém 50,01% de participação, em parceria com o FI-FGTS (49,99%). O empreendimento conta com duas turbinas de 25,5 MW e área alagada de 23.46 km². A obra, iniciada em Outubro de 2007, gerou empregos e desenvolvimento aos municípios de Rolador e Salvador das Missões, no RS. (Portuguese Only)

O empreendimento conta com duas turbinas de 25,5 MW e área alagada de 23.46 km².

A obra, iniciada em Outubro de 2007, gerou empregos e desenvolvimento aos municípios de Rolador e Salvador das Missões, no RS.
